note: Per-platform engine artifacts, downloaded on first run. The installer is ~37 MB and does NOT carry the engine: it is ~300 MB compressed, and embedding it made the installer 330 MB against competitors shipping under 50 MB. Served from lobrowser.com rather than GitHub so the whole install path stays on one origin we control. LOBSTER_ENGINE_URL/LOBSTER_ENGINE_SHA256 override this for testing/self-hosting. A platform with no entry fails provisioning with a clear error rather than downloading another OS's archive.
staleKeyMeaning: An OPTIONAL 'stale' string on a platform entry means the repo itself asserts those bytes must not be shipped, and its value says why. It is NOT a comment. engine_provision.rs deliberately does not read it - a user who already holds this manifest should still be able to provision rather than be stranded - so it is enforced at BUILD time instead: scripts/build-windows-product.ps1 prints a red do-not-ship warning when the win-x64 entry carries one. scripts/bump-engine-version.mjs clears it when the platform is genuinely published, and logs what it cleared.

win-x64.stale: REBUILD REQUIRED before this entry is correct, and the archive is NOT uploaded: this URL returned HTTP 404 when checked from the Windows host on 2026-08-26, so Windows first-run provisioning cannot succeed today. These bytes are also wrong on their own terms - verified by inspecting the published archive, chrome.dll contains 11 of the 13 lobium-* switch strings and is missing exactly 'lobium-device-frame' and 'lobium-device-screen', so an Android profile opens with no phone stage. The cause is NOT that the build predates the fix (the publishing commit's tree already contained it; the two timestamps in the older write-up were in different timezones): the archive was built from an older tree than the commit that published it. The device frame was additionally Linux-only in source until 2026-08-26, so a rebuild alone would not have fixed it - branding/device-frame.patch now compiles its BrowserView call sites on Windows too. See docs/qa/2026-08-26-windows-understanding.md.
